title: The Atlas defines bounty scope, severity and rewards by reference to Immunefi's external listings rather than fixing them in text
content:
Across A.2.11.1.1.2.1 through A.2.11.1.1.3.2 the Atlas repeatedly declines to state the substance. Assets in Scope, Impacts in Scope, out-of-scope vulnerabilities, feasibility limits, PoC requirements, researcher eligibility restrictions, and the reward tables per threat level are all "specified on Sky's listing on the Immunefi platform," with URLs. Severity uses "[t]he Immunefi Vulnerability Severity Classification System," and A.2.11.1.1.2.2 authorizes the Protocol Security Workstream Lead "to adopt a new severity system ... in consultation with relevant technical stakeholders."

This is deliberate incorporation by reference to a mutable external source, and the reason is operational tempo. Scope changes with every deployment; a severity table amended by Atlas Edit would lag reality and turn routine security maintenance into a governance queue.

The cost is that the Atlas ceases to be a complete statement of the program. A reader cannot determine from the Atlas what is covered or what a critical finding pays, and the effective terms can change without any Sky governance action — Immunefi "is the party responsible for conducting the Bug Bounty Program; its setup and operations are based on standards set by Immunefi" (A.2.11.1.1.1).

The accountability that remains is role-based: the Protocol Security Workstream Lead "is responsible for maintaining these lists of Assets In Scope, in consultation with the relevant stakeholders." Note the asymmetry the same provisions create — for Sky Core, scope includes "smart contracts, frontend applications, data infrastructure and oracles," while for SparkLend it "only include[s] smart contracts."
description: Assets, impacts, exclusions, severity classification and reward tables all live on the Immunefi platform, and the Protocol Security Workstream Lead may adopt an entirely new severity system.
